feature: A capture in the history strip is never stretched and never a mile wide
summary: The capture history strip stops lying about the shape of a picture. A very wide capture is cropped to two and a half to one instead of running on for most of the strip, and a capture smaller than the row is drawn at the size it really is instead of being blown up soft. The same two rules now hold for the capture toast.
setup: Photonz Dev, capture history (Capture > Show History, or shift-command-H). Nothing to turn on: the rules apply to every tile. To see all the shapes at once, run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/history-thumbnail-shapes-walk.json, which lends the strip six fixture captures and takes them back afterwards.

try.do: Press shift-command-H to drop the history strip down.
Find a very wide capture (a nav bar, a table header, a full-width toolbar). It should be a 2.5:1 tile keeping the LEFT end of the picture, with its right edge fading out.
Compare that against the same strip before the change.
Find a small capture, something like a 60 by 30 badge. It should be a small crisp chip in the middle of the row, not a blurry tile filling the whole row height.
Hover that small chip. The action buttons should still appear under it, and the whole slot around it should still be clickable.
Arrow along to it with the left and right keys. The accent ring should hug the picture, not a box of empty space around it.
Find a very tall narrow capture. It should now show the TOP of the picture at a readable width, with its bottom edge fading out, instead of a hairline.
Find a recording. The play badge should sit in the middle of the cropped tile and the duration pill in its bottom right corner.

evaluate: Is 2.5:1 the right stopping point for a wide capture, or would 3:1 still read as one picture rather than a band?
A wide capture keeps its LEFT end on the theory that the start of a bar is what you recognise it by. Does that hold for the wide things you actually capture, or do you look for the right end?
A small capture is now a small chip floating in the row. Is that honest and fine, or does it read as broken next to full-height neighbours?
The cut edge of a cropped tile fades out. Did you notice that at all, and does a thumbnail even need to say it is cropped?
Tall narrow captures are now cropped from the top too, which is more than was asked for. Better, or would you rather they stayed whole and tiny?
rough: The fade that marks a cropped edge is a soft darkening, so on a dark screenshot it is close to invisible. It reads on light captures and disappears on dark ones, which is not a great way to say something.

Tall captures being cropped from the top is a deliberate extension beyond what was reported. The report was only about wide captures and about blowing small ones up. The sliver a tall capture used to draw was so thin nothing was legible in it, and one rule at both ends is simpler than a rule at one end and a workaround at the other, but it is a visible change you did not ask for and it is easy to put back.

The capture toast now obeys the same rules, but there is no way to drive a toast from a playtest walk, so that half was proved by the tested sizing rule and a build rather than by a picture. The common case (an ordinary screenshot filling the 196 by 124 box) is unchanged by arithmetic.

A recording reports a scale of 1, because an MP4 carries no DPI tag the way a PNG does. That is harmless today (a poster frame is always far bigger than a tile, so the never-upscale rule never fires on one) but a tiny recording would be drawn twice the size it should be.
